sections.title: Behavioural rounds at this level

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: No guide of yours covers this, so this page was written for the site, as of October 2026. Tools and versions change quickly: check the official documentation before relying on details.

blocks: Interviewers look for ownership and honesty, and for experienced candidates, influence and mentoring too. Prepare stories before the interview: inventing one live rarely goes well.

rows: What you did, and why: use "I"
The outcome in numbers, and what you learned
blocks.caption: Most weak answers spend their time on the situation.

sections.title: Stories to prepare
blocks: Your `10-Interview-Prep` plan lists teamwork, conflict, failure, learning fast and taking the lead. As a fresher, draw on college projects, internships and team work. The last four below are what experienced candidates are asked, so prepare them when you have the stories.

rows: A conflict with a colleague or manager
A failure or production mistake you caused
Taking the lead without being asked
Pushing back on a requirement or deadline
Paying down technical debt: how you justified it
A design you changed after feedback
60 to 90 seconds: current work, strengths, why this role
Moving towards something; never criticise your employer
Specifics from your research: product, stack, challenges
A real weakness and what you are doing about it
A direction that fits this role
A researched range, after you understand the role
Ask about on-call, how decisions get made, and team challenges

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Prepare 8 to 10 stories that can each answer several questions.
- Spend most of the time on your actions.
- End with a measurable result and a lesson.
- Practise aloud and time yourself.

items.question: What is wrong with "we had a tight deadline and the team worked hard and delivered"?
items.answer: No personal action, no specific decision and no measurable result.

items.question: How do you describe a failure without hurting yourself?
items.answer: Choose a real but recoverable one. Own it, then spend most of the answer on how you fixed it and what you changed afterwards.
